design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable FPGA top-level bounded active-aero control wrapper around an external NVIDIA DoMINO-based software/GPU surrogate transport. The RTL provides configuration, request/response transport, response validation, timeout and stale detection, deterministic safe fallback, bounded actuation, and status reporting without implementing surrogate inference, CFD, mesh, or tensor processing.
design_summary.operating_model: Single synchronous clk domain with active-low synchronous reset rst_n. Control and status use a compact 8-bit CSR address / 64-bit data window. External model transport uses 128-bit valid/ready request and response streams. The top-level logic launches requests when enabled and idle, tracks sequence state and pending status, validates and decodes responses, clamps and optionally rate-limits actuator commands, and drives safe fallback behavior on fault or communication loss.

external_interfaces.name: CSR control/status window
external_interfaces.intent: Software-readable and writable configuration and status access for enable, diagnostic mode, timeout and stale thresholds, sequence seed, bounds, rate limiting, fallback mode, and status clear.

external_interfaces.name: Model request transport
external_interfaces.intent: RTL-driven outbound request frame transport to the external CPU/GPU surrogate service; valid and data are outputs, ready is an input.

external_interfaces.name: Model response transport
external_interfaces.intent: Inbound response transport from the external CPU/GPU surrogate service; valid and data are inputs, ready is an output.

external_interfaces.name: Actuation and fault outputs
external_interfaces.intent: Bounded active-aero command output and compact fault summary for software and downstream actuator logic.

external_interfaces.name: Debug and verification hooks
external_interfaces.intent: Synthesis-friendly observability for sequence tracking, timeout expiration, stale detection, and clamp events.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Single synthesizable FPGA top module implementing bounded active-aero control around an external surrogate transport.
responsibilities: Implement CSR readable and writable configuration registers for enable, diagnostic mode, request timeout threshold, stale-data threshold, sequence counter seed, actuation min/max bounds, rate-limit enable, fallback mode select, and status clear.
Generate and hold req_valid and req_data until req_ready is observed, with req_data stable during the entire valid/ready wait.
Latch the outstanding request sequence number when a request is launched and keep request_pending asserted until a matching response is accepted or timeout occurs.
Drive rsp_ready from RTL according to request-pending and safe-receive policy, and accept rsp_data only on rsp_valid and rsp_ready handshake.
Validate response sequence against the outstanding request sequence and mark stale on mismatch or when response age exceeds the configured threshold.
Mark invalid_response when response status bits indicate malformed, unsupported, or otherwise invalid payload format.
On timeout, stale, invalid_response, envelope_violation, or communication loss, enter fallback and drive a deterministic safe command.
Support at least two safe_fallback_manager modes: hold-last-safe and predefined-safe-posture.
Clamp actuator commands to CSR-configured min/max bounds and optionally rate-limit command changes; raise envelope_violation or clamp status when clipping occurs.
Provide deterministic startup behavior with safe fallback outputs until configuration is complete and a valid response is accepted.
Expose debug and verification hooks for request/response sequence tracking, timeout expiration, stale detection, and clamp events.
Remain synthesizable and FPGA-friendly with only small control/status storage plus optional technology-neutral block RAM for limited response history buffering.
interface_notes: All external top-level ports are inherited exactly as specified in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON and are not renamed.
Top-level outputs listed in must_drive are driven by RTL logic in this module, not by child inputs alone.

The request payload is compact and carries only contract fields such as sequence tag, flow-condition summary, vehicle-state summary, geometry descriptor token or pointer, and control flags; raw geometry, tensors, meshes, and flow fields are excluded.
The response decoder uses only the defined contract fields and status bits; surrogate inference is explicitly out of scope.
Any bulk response history or FIFO storage is described through the technology-neutral fpga_block_ram_generic wrapper and not flattened into registers.
ownership_notes: Owns request sequencing, timeout and age counters, CSR decode, response validation, command bounding, safe fallback selection, and status flag generation.

Owns the RTL drivers for req_valid, req_data, rsp_ready, act_cmd_valid, act_cmd_data, fault_status, debug_seq_request, debug_seq_response, debug_timeout_expired, debug_stale_detected, and debug_clamp_event.
Does not own req_ready, rsp_valid, or rsp_data, which are external inputs.
Does not own any surrogate inference, CFD computation, mesh processing, tensor manipulation, or large payload storage logic beyond the compact transport contract.

data_flow_summary: Software writes configuration through cfg_addr/cfg_wdata/cfg_we; the top module updates enable, diagnostic mode, thresholds, sequence seed, actuation bounds, rate-limit control, fallback mode select, and status clear behavior.

When enabled and not busy, the top module assembles req_data[127:0] with sequence tag, compact flow and vehicle summaries, geometry descriptor token, and control flags, then asserts req_valid until req_ready is observed.
While req_valid is high and req_ready is low, req_data remains stable and the outstanding request sequence is held in internal state.
On acceptance of a request, the module marks request_pending and busy, initializes or advances sequence tracking, and begins response-age monitoring.
The top module drives rsp_ready according to safe receive policy and outstanding request state; response data is only consumed on rsp_valid and rsp_ready handshake.
On response acceptance, the module decodes compact response fields, validates the response sequence, evaluates status bits, and determines whether the response is valid, stale, or invalid.
A valid response updates the candidate active-aero command, which is then clamped to the configured min/max bounds and optionally rate-limited before output.
If a response is stale, invalid, late, or mismatched, or if request/response communication is lost, the module asserts the relevant fault flags and transitions to deterministic fallback behavior.

The safe fallback manager selects either hold-last-safe or predefined-safe-posture behavior and controls whether act_cmd_valid remains asserted with a safe command or deasserts while fallback is active.
Optional response history storage, if used, is implemented via fpga_block_ram_generic with native block RAM mapping and limited depth, preserving FPGA-friendly storage usage.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain clk at 50.0 MHz nominal period 20 ns. All state machines are synchronous to clk and use fixed-width arithmetic and explicit registered state transitions.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low and synchronous in the selected coding style. On reset, control registers initialize to a safe configuration with enable deasserted, request and response state cleared, fallback active, act_cmd_valid deasserted, act_cmd_data driven to the deterministic safe fallback posture, req_valid deasserted, rsp_ready set according to safe receive policy, cfg_rdata cleared, and fault/debug indicators cleared or set to safe deterministic reset values. Outputs remain in safe fallback until software programs the configuration and a valid response is accepted.

integration_notes: The design is intended for FPGA prototype integration with an external CPU/GPU surrogate service and is suitable for Arch2RTL translation into synthesizable RTL.
The interface is intentionally compact: 64-bit CSR accesses and 128-bit streaming payloads only; no geometry arrays, meshes, tensors, or flow fields appear as individual pins.
Any implementation of response history, small queues, or buffering should be technology-neutral and infer FPGA block RAM rather than large register banks.
Do not introduce additional hierarchy, rename modules, rename ports, or change filenames; this document is descriptive only.
The top-level module name, port list, and rtl_output_file remain exactly as specified in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The selected FPGA memory contract is represented by fpga_block_ram_generic / u_response_history_ram with 16x128 storage, if used for limited history buffering.
consistency_notes: Hierarchy, ports, and filenames are inherited from digital_spec_json.
No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
